newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police hunt Kurd rebel jail escapees.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police hunt Kurd rebel jail escapees.

text.p: Police hunted on Monday for 20 fugitive prisoners, mostly Kurdish rebels, who tunnelled their way out of a high-security jail in southern Turkey at the weekend, local officials said.
"The search is going on but there are no developments," a spokesman for the governor's office in the town on Antakya told Reuters.
Sixteen Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels serving long terms were among the escapees, who fled through an 80-metre (260-foot) tunnel at Iskenderun jail on Friday night.
Jail officials have calculated it took six months to dig the tunnel. The remaining four convicts who fled were members of a far-left guerrilla group.
Authorities estimate there are 10,000 people in Turkish jails for links to the PKK, fighting for Kurdish self-rule in southeast Turkey.
More than 21,000 people have died in the 12-year conflict.
